rules.title: Line amount, line discount and net total
rules.statement: A line's amount is its quantity times its rate. A line discount percentage lowers the rate from the list price (rate = list price times one minus the discount). The net total is the sum of the line amounts.
rules.formula:
rate       = price_list_rate * (1 - discount_percentage / 100)
amount     = qty * rate
net_total  = sum(amount)

rules.title: Taxes by charge type, with a running total
rules.statement: Each tax row has a charge type. "On Net Total" applies its rate to the net total. "On Previous Row Amount" applies its rate to the tax amount of the row it points to. "On Previous Row Total" applies its rate to the running total of that row (net total plus every tax up to it), which makes taxes compound. "Actual" adds a fixed amount and is not a base for the "On Net Total" rows. Each row carries a running total; the grand total is the net total plus all taxes.
rules.formula:
On Net Total:           tax = net_total * rate
On Previous Row Amount: tax = tax_of(row_id) * rate
On Previous Row Total:  tax = total_of(row_id) * rate
Actual:                 tax = fixed amount
total(row) = total(previous row, or net_total) + tax(row)
grand_total = net_total + sum(tax)

given.taxes: 10% On Net Total, then 5% On Previous Row Total of row 1
10% On Net Total, then 50% On Previous Row Amount of row 1

contradictions: When two tax rows use the same tax account, the earlier row was computed with the later row's rate (R-007): the cascade examples above use two different accounts.

rules.title: Discount on the whole invoice
rules.statement: A discount percentage can apply to the whole invoice, either on the net total or on the grand total. On the net total it lowers the base before taxes. On the grand total it is computed on the amount including tax and spread back so that the net total and the taxes both shrink. With a single tax on the net total, both give the same totals.
rules.formula:
on Net Total:   net_total = sum(amount) * (1 - pct);  taxes on the reduced net
on Grand Total: discount = grand_total_before * pct;  net and taxes reduced so grand_total = before - discount
rules.notes: Observed with one tax on the net total only. With a fixed charge or a compound tax, the two modes should differ; that case is not observed yet (U-002).

rules.title: Price that already includes the tax
rules.statement: A tax row can be marked as included in the price. The rate typed on the line is then the price including tax, and the program works the net amount back from it: net = price including tax divided by one plus the tax rate.
rules.formula:
net_amount = qty * rate_incl_tax / (1 + tax_rate)
tax = qty * rate_incl_tax - net_amount

rules.title: Rounding of amounts (banker's rounding to the cent)
rules.statement: Amounts are rounded to the currency's precision (two decimals here) with banker's rounding: a value exactly halfway goes to the even digit. The method is a system setting. The rounded total is rounded to the smallest currency unit (the cent), so 40.50 stays 40.50 on this site.
rules.formula:
round(x) = round_half_to_even(x, 2)        # system setting "Banker's Rounding"
rounded_total = round to the smallest currency fraction
rules.notes: Round-half-up would give 0.63 and 0.13 in the first two examples. The method can be changed in the system settings; a rebuild must read it from its own settings, not hard-code it.

rules.title: Whole quantities for units that require them
rules.statement: Each unit of measure says whether its quantities must be whole numbers. A line with a fractional quantity in such a unit (for example 2.5 "Nos") is refused with an error naming the row; the same quantity in a unit that allows fractions (for example kilograms) is accepted.
rules.formula: if uom.must_be_whole_number and qty is not an integer: refuse ("row N: quantity cannot be a fraction")

rules.title: Two tax rows on the same tax account share one rate
rules.statement: When two tax rows of an invoice use the same tax account, the earlier "On Net Total" row was computed with the rate of the later row, not with its own. Observed twice; the cause (one rate kept per account) is not established.
rules.formula: observed: rows on the same account -> the "On Net Total" row uses the last row's rate

given.taxes: 10% On Net Total + 5% On Previous Row Total, same account
10% On Net Total + 50% On Previous Row Amount, same account

rules.notes: The behaviour is observed; why it happens is a hypothesis (U-001). A rebuild should keep one tax account per tax row and flag duplicate accounts, rather than copy a behaviour whose intent is unknown.

features.title: Create a sales invoice with discounts and taxes

refuses a fractional quantity in a whole-number unit
